sourceOverrides.scope: Temporary server-only instrumentation. Existing main/load rejection handlers log; fetch catch records then rethrows the same error. No production files modified.

instrumentation.description: Separate fixture server serves one exact hashed host variant. Existing main rejection ownership and load catch log operation IDs; the fetch catch records and rethrows the identical error. Lifecycle logs retain per-document identities. No Playwright request routing, published runtime, or stable qualification script changed.
instrumentation.limits: The temporary instrumentation can affect scheduling. It proves only the recorded variant/event; it does not retroactively classify all unchanged-production errors or upgrade their failed receipts. Per-document observer initialization also runs in child frames; classification below uses the main document ID verified by the prior successful ordinary-entry snapshot.

events.classified: Matched old-document fetch rejection with an existing load owner during ordinary navigation.

timelineUTC.event: Native fetch starts for the exact URL; AbortSignal is not aborted
Playwright receives the native access-control pageerror for that URL
Fetch rejects with TypeError: Load failed; catch records then rethrows same error; existing load catch receives operation114
Existing host.close runs; no pending load remains

events.interpretation: The application had not reached its pagehide cleanup when this already-owned optional artwork load failed. The matching native request failure propagates through the existing load catch, whose cleanup executes before rethrow. Static app.mjs:2544 catch consumes the load chain and chooses the existing artwork fallback; this final app catch was not separately instrumented. The fresh page enters ordinary mode with unchanged observed persistence.
events.notClaimed: No proof that every access-control diagnostic has this cause, no error suppression, no claim that beforeunload cancellation semantics should replace ordinary pagehide cleanup.

events.classified: Unresolved native/JavaScript diagnostic during the old-document teardown interval.
events.observed: Received after the old document host.close and before next document initialization. It has no stack, matching host operation, or delivered DOM error/unhandledrejection event in this sample.
events.notClaimed: Temporal association and absent DOM events are insufficient to prove harmless cancellation or to exempt the error. The strict failure remains.

additionalObservations: Reloads1 and4 logged native createImageBitmap InvalidStateError rejections in the pre-existing main rejection handler and load catch after beforeunload, without a corresponding pageerror. Therefore native rejection and pageerror are not equivalent observables.
The receipt also retains ordinary source-preview build-info404 and external soundtrack CSP console diagnostics separately. These are not silently dropped or classified as the native pageerrors.

primarySources.finding: Installed Playwright1.62.1 uses WebKit revision2336/browser26.5; pinned upstream base is343e13bf22dca9d0ec227801419aab0f9001a32f.
An error-level console message in the JavaScript source category is converted to pageerror. This transport does not require a DOM error or unhandledrejection event.
The native loader creates the observed fetch/blob access-control message and logs it in the JavaScript error console category independently of application promise handling.
logErrorAndFail logs the native loader error before notifying the client of request failure, consistent with this observed ordering.

The exact Context is stopped text occurs when JSON-response construction or response cloning lacks a context global object. Those possible sites do not establish this event’s actual origin; no direct corresponding use was found in the observed host/app chain. The inspected file set is not an exhaustive WebKit source search.

nextStep: No production remediation is justified by the classified fetch event.
